headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Roo Code’s workspace write/network/MCP access can collide with Plane’s file-backed issue/task workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP; Plane accepts file uploads and handles hyperlinks/notes. If Plane content is copied into Roo Code or surfaced through shared files, prompt-like instructions can be injected into Roo Code’s tool loop. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Plane issue text or uploaded files are fed into Roo Code without provenance tagging, injection risk exists.
IF Roo Code is configured to act on file or MCP content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Plane exports into Roo Code.
Require a human review step before Roo Code acts on Plane text.
Strip instructions from uploaded files before handoff.
Use separate workspaces for Plane artifacts and Roo Code tasks.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes, while Roo Code has broad network egress, reads workspace files, and can use MCP. In default self-hosted VS Code use, shared filesystem access plus outbound model/API calls can leak sensitive workspace or ticket data outside the intended boundary.
conditions: IF Plane artifacts are stored in the same workspace that Roo Code reads, leakage is possible.
IF Roo Code sends workspace context to a configured model API or MCP server, sensitive ticket/file contents can leave the host.
mitigations: Keep Plane data in a separate directory from Roo Code workspaces.
Turn off or restrict Roo Code network egress for sensitive projects.
Avoid placing secrets or customer files in shared workspace folders.
Review MCP server allowlists before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane is not write_filesystem-capable, but Roo Code can write files, modify git state, and share state via filesystem across instances. If Plane-managed files are mirrored into the same workspace, Roo Code can overwrite or race on artifacts and git state without coordination. The conflict is one-sided but still dangerous because Roo Code has the mutable surface.
conditions: IF Plane artifacts are mirrored into a Roo Code workspace, concurrent edits can clobber them.
IF multiple Roo Code instances touch the same git repo, uncoordinated commits or rewrites can occur.
mitigations: Use one Roo Code instance per repository.
Lock the repo before automated edits.
Keep Plane exports read-only in a separate folder.
Pause git automation while Plane artifacts are being imported.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transaction coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane manages issues and tasks, and Roo Code can act on workspace files and browser state. If Plane output is copied into Roo Code as authoritative task context, Roo Code may propagate mistakes into code or commits. The pair does not show a built-in verification loop, but the downstream harm is limited to workflow errors rather than guaranteed external action.
conditions: IF Plane issue descriptions are treated as ground truth by Roo Code, errors can cascade into code changes.
IF Roo Code commits or edits based on unverified Plane tasks, incorrect work products can be produced.
mitigations: Require a second reviewer for Plane-to-code handoffs.
Ask Roo Code to restate assumptions before editing.
Compare generated changes against the original Plane ticket.
Limit Roo Code to draft-only mode for imported tasks.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Plane is an issue/task system that can hold files, notes, and roadmaps; Roo Code handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys. If regulated data is placed in Plane and then opened in Roo Code, retention and residency controls may diverge. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so this is a policy-gap risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Plane and then processed in Roo Code, policy mismatch risk exists.
IF Roo Code sends screenshots or code context to a third-party model API, residency/retention obligations may be affected.
mitigations: Classify data before placing it in Plane.
Do not use Roo Code on regulated tickets without approval.
Review model-provider retention settings.
Keep secrets out of shared issue text and screenshots.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both tools.
